first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ and activation is down 6% QoQ—both point to friction in early user experience. Memory_31 and memory_86 demonstrate that signup simplification and shortened onboarding have proven durable lift in activation and time-to-value. Verifying these two will confirm the mechanism and baseline effect sizes before committing resources. Simplify_onboarding directly addresses both current performance gaps and is upstream of revenue quality—reducing friction improves conversion without artificially lowering price or diluting brand. This preserves long-term unit economics better than promotional_pricing (which competes on margin against the entrant and may attract less loyal cohorts) or referral_incentive (which adds acquisition cost and is better suited to growth phases, not recovery). Enterprise_sales_assist is orthogonal to the SMB activation problem. Activation_messaging is a lighter lever, but onboarding friction is the root cause. A standard_experiment on signup/onboarding simplification can run in parallel with market monitoring and poses manageable downside risk while addressing the mechanical problem in the data.

final.rationale: Archive confirms both memories with strong effect sizes: exp_31 showed +9% activation and +4% qualified revenue on SMB with only -1% retention risk; exp_86 showed +13% completion and +3% retention lift with faster time-to-value. The 4% QoQ onboarding completion decline and 6% activation decline directly match the levers these experiments validated. Simplify_onboarding is mechanically sound, segment-appropriate (SMB is price-sensitive competitor target), and carries proven retention safety. The small retention dip in exp_31 is offset by the +3% gain in exp_86, suggesting the combined approach (simpler signup + shorter flow) nets positive retention. This strategy addresses root friction rather than competing on price margin, preserves brand positioning, and targets qualified revenue sustainably. Standard_experiment scale allows real-time learning before broader rollout. Activation_messaging alone would be insufficient given the magnitude of decline; promotional_pricing would erode margins against entrant without addressing activation mechanics.
